$comment: Enemy pressure, from GDD section 7.1. The bundle - three waves - is the unit of pressure, not the single wave. Timing is scheduled; composition is procedural: which enemies, where they enter and how many are rolled, but WHEN they arrive is a design knob rather than a random one. The hard cap of three live wave-groups is exactly one full bundle, so ignoring a whole bundle puts the player at maximum pressure with the next one inbound.
$pacing_comment: The canon pacing is tuned for a PC session. On a phone, a 30-minute gap between bundles means most players would finish a session without ever meeting one, so 'mobile' is active by default and compresses the schedule while keeping every ratio canon holds meaningful - three waves to a bundle, the gap timed from the END of the previous bundle so a struggling player is not punished, and one bundle live at a time. Switch activePacing to 'canon' to play the PC timings.
$composition_comment: Rolled per wave. Minotaur scarcity is the tuning knob that makes tier 2 mean anything, and the scythe-bearer is rarer still - canon is explicit that 'only a few' is what gives them weight.

ambient.$comment: A separate population that persists between bundles. Never includes tier 3.

$stealth_comment: Enemies do not know where the player is; hiding or moving carefully lets exploration continue indefinitely, and the player is never required to clear a wave. During the FIRST bundle only, every enemy is shown - a tutorial affordance that then fades, because enemies not knowing where you are only matters if you do not automatically know where they are.
